Special case: for "Avg SLA" metric, down is good — check `metric.id === "k05"` and flip colors. Keep it simple: add a `isInverse` derivation or just hardcode for k05. - Icon bg: `size-8 rounded-md bg-primary/10 text-primary flex items-center justify-center` ### 2. `components/dashboard/quick-actions.tsx` (server component) Hero card with gradient top accent: - Wrap in a `

"New request" — primary button — icon Plus 2. "Invite client" — outline button — icon UserPlus 3. "Generate AI brief" — outline button — icon Sparkles — add a small "AI" badge on the right (pill with `bg-primary/10 text-primary text-[10px] font-semibold px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded`) - All buttons full width - Buttons are non-functional — don't attach onClick ### 3. `components/dashboard/sla-warnings.tsx` (server component) - Card with header "SLA warnings" + small description "Requests approaching or past deadline" - Compute the list: import `requests` and `clients` from mock, filter via `getSlaStatus(r.slaDueAt)` where status is `"warning" | "breached"`, sort breached first, take top 4. - For each: row with: - Left: small colored dot (breached=red, warning=amber) - Middle: request title (truncate), below it tiny text "ClientCompany · 2h overdue" or "ClientCompany · due in 5h" - Right: "View" ghost button - If empty (shouldn't happen with current mock), render EmptyState: icon Clock, heading "All clear", description "No SLA breaches right now", no action button - Time formatting: small helper inline — compute hours diff from the fixed anchor `new Date("2026-04-10T12:00:00Z")` to `slaDueAt`. Simplest: mark `"use client"` so onClick works when passed. ### 6. `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` — replace placeholder ```tsx export default function DashboardPage() { return ( <> {/* KPI grid: 5 cards on lg, 2 cols on md, 1 on mobile */}
{kpiMetrics.map((m, i) => )}
{/* 2-col: left 2/3 QuickActions, right 1/3 SlaWarnings */}
); } ``` Wait — re-read: plan says "Left (2/3): QuickActions" and "Right (1/3): SlaWarnings". But QuickActions is a small hero card — it shouldn't be 2/3 width of tall empty space. Better layout: make the left col a wrapper holding QuickActions on top and maybe reserved space. Actually, do what the plan says for now (2/3 / 1/3). QuickActions will have natural height; just let the column grow. Use `lg:col-span-2` for QuickActions and let SlaWarnings be single col. Fine. ### 7. Verification ``` cd ~/Clientloop pnpm tsc --noEmit pnpm lint pnpm build pnpm dev & # briefly curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" localhost:3000/dashboard # expect 200 # kill dev ``` All must pass. Build must succeed. ### 8. Commit ``` git add -A && git commit -m "feat(dashboard): home with KPIs, quick actions, SLA warnings, activity feed" ``` ## Hard rules - NO `any`, NO `@ts-ignore`, NO `as X` assertions - NO hardcoded hex colors (emerald-600 / rose-600 Tailwind utilities are OK — they're theme-adjacent) - All icon maps must be typed (use `Record` or a switch with exhaustive typing) - KPI card animation MUST use `animationFillMode: "both"` — without it cards flash before animation - Use existing components (`Card`, `Button`, `Avatar`) from `components/ui/*` - Do NOT install new dependencies - Import path alias is `@/*` - Use `next/image` only if you load remote images (not needed here — avatars are SVG/initials based) ## Report back (under 300 words) - Files created/modified - tsc/lint/build output (pass/fail) - curl /dashboard status - Commit hash - Deviations with reasoning

1	# Clientloop — Phase 1 UI Shell Plan
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Clientloop is the codename (from Phase 18 dossier candidates) for the ManyRequests-style SaaS already researched across 22 phases in the Boldteq dossier (`ManyRequestsDossier.jsx`). The dossier returned a **conditional GO** with a hard gate at Phase 15: 300 waitlist + 10 paid LOIs before writing code.
6	
7	Yash is **intentionally overriding** the gate for a narrow purpose: build the **UI shell only** (mock data, no backend, no auth wiring) so it can be **used as the clickable validation asset** Phase 15 already requires (Figma-alternative prototype for LOI interviews). This is the cheapest path to satisfy the gate without wasting build effort later — the shell becomes real production code once the gate passes.
8	
9	**What we are building in Phase 1:**
10	- Agency-side UI shell for Clientloop
11	- Next.js 15 App Router + TypeScript (strict, no `any`) + Tailwind + shadcn/ui
12	- Three working screens: Dashboard Home, Request Inbox (table + Kanban toggle), Clients/Services/Settings
13	- All data mocked in `lib/mock/` — zero backend, zero auth, zero DB
14	- Fully responsive, dark-mode capable, production-quality look
15	- Deployable to Vercel as a static demo on day 1
16	
17	**What we are NOT building:**
18	- No Clerk, Neon, Prisma, Razorpay, Stripe, Claude API, tRPC
19	- No Request Detail + AI Brief screen (deferred — dossier's hero feature, but not in this pass per user selection)
20	- No client-facing portal (agency side only)
21	- No landing page / marketing site (separate Quill work later)
22	
23	**Why it matters:** the dossier's wedge is AI request-to-brief + flat pricing + Razorpay. The UI shell must *look* like a product that ships those things, even though none are wired. Visuals sell the LOIs.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Name & Branding
28	
29	- **Product name (Phase 1):** Clientloop
30	- **Rationale:** shortest, most pronounceable of the 10 candidates, and the word "loop" ties directly to Phase 21's client-invite viral loop (the actual growth engine)
31	- **Trademark risk:** NOT cleared — dossier flags CHECK gate. Treat name as provisional. Use it in UI, but do not register domains or trademarks yet
32	- **Wordmark:** plain text `Clientloop` in Inter bold for v1, no logo commissioned yet
33	- **Primary color:** Violet (`#6d28d9`) — already used in the dossier artifact header, carries forward as brand accent
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Architecture Decision: Scaffold Fresh
38	
39	Confirmed via Explore agent: no existing Next.js projects in Yash's active portfolio. Rankora and CROBOT are both Vite+React+React Router (Lovable-origin) — not migratable to Next.js 15 App Router. shadcn components and Tailwind tokens are portable; everything else is a rewrite.
40	
41	**Decision:** `pnpm create next-app@latest Clientloop` at `~/Clientloop`. Copy token structure from Rankora's Tailwind config but nothing else.
42	
43	**Memory impact:** create `~/.claude/memory/stacks/saas-nextjs-15.md` after scaffold so the next Next.js SaaS inherits these patterns. (Mira runs this after Phase 1 completes.)
44	
45	---
46	
47	## Directory Layout
48	
49	```

117	---
118	
119	## Implementation Steps
120	
121	### Step 1 — Scaffold & Tokens (Riko)

124	2. `cd Clientloop && pnpm dlx shadcn@latest init` → New York style, neutral base, CSS variables, `--radius: 0.75rem`
